f.title: Kidney Injury TAG is generated on clinical reviewer request (kidney signal or kidney injury AESI)
f.statement: The Kidney Injury Targeted Analysis Guide (TAG) gives more in-depth analyses to investigate a potential kidney injury signal, or kidney injury that is an adverse event of special interest (AESI). It is generated when the clinical reviewer requests it.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND Standard Safety Tables and Figures, Kidney Injury TAG v1.2): marketing applications with a potential kidney injury signal or kidney injury as an AESI; informative for applicants, not binding on them
f.processes: Signal detection; Signal management; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
The goal of the Standard Safety Tables and
Figures Kidney Injury Targeted Analysis Guide (TAG) is to provide more in-depth
analyses to investigate a potential kidney injury signal or when kidney injury is an
adverse event of special interest (AESI). The kidney injury TAG is generated upon
request by the clinical reviewer.

f.title: Kidney TAG analyses are exploratory; extra custom analyses may be requested at reviewer discretion
f.statement: Targeted analyses in the Kidney Injury TAG are exploratory and not exhaustive. Additional custom analyses to characterize the potential for kidney injury may be requested, and the clinical reviewer decides which tables and figures go into the clinical safety review.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND Standard Safety Tables and Figures, Kidney Injury TAG v1.2): marketing applications with a potential kidney injury signal or kidney injury as an AESI; informative for applicants, not binding on them

rows.quote:
Targeted analyses are provided for exploratory purposes and are not meant to be
exhaustive. Additional custom analyses not included in the TAG to further characterize
the potential for kidney injury may also be requested. The determination of which tables
and figures for inclusion in the clinical safety review is at the discretion of the clinical
reviewer.

f.title: Consider additional kidney analyses for abnormal or changing muscle mass and pre-existing kidney disease
f.statement: Additional analyses may be needed to understand kidney injury risk in populations with unusual muscle mass (for example muscular dystrophy) or muscle mass that changes during the trial (for example ICU populations), where creatinine-based assessments may not reliably measure kidney function, and in populations with pre-existing kidney disease or prone to frequent variation in kidney function (for example heart failure).
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND Standard Safety Tables and Figures, Kidney Injury TAG v1.2): marketing applications with a potential kidney injury signal or kidney injury as an AESI; informative for applicants, not binding on them
f.processes: Signal detection; Signal management; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
Additional analyses may be needed to understand the risk of kidney injury in the
following situations:
    •    Populations with unusual muscle mass (e.g., muscular dystrophy) or muscle mass

         populations) for which creatinine-based assessments may not provide an
         accurate or reliable measure of kidney function.
    •    Populations with pre-existing kidney disease or those prone to frequent variations
         in kidney function (e.g., heart failure).

f.title: Consider additional analyses for late-onset kidney injury or creatinine changes without loss of function
f.statement: Additional analyses may also be needed when drug-induced kidney injury does not show as an early decline in kidney function, or when the drug changes serum creatinine without changing kidney function (for example by altering tubular secretion of creatinine). They may include subgroup analyses by AKI risk factors (for example baseline kidney function where much of the population has CKD, age, use of ACE inhibitors, ARBs or diuretics); other kidney laboratory data (for example quantitative proteinuria or albuminuria, cystatin C); and other signs suggesting a mechanism, such as concurrent decreases in blood pressure and albuminuria that could indicate a hemodynamic effect.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND Standard Safety Tables and Figures, Kidney Injury TAG v1.2): marketing applications with a potential kidney injury signal or kidney injury as an AESI; informative for applicants, not binding on them

f.title: Do not use BUN changes to detect changes in kidney function or kidney injury
f.statement: Blood urea nitrogen (BUN) is a less useful indicator than serum creatinine or eGFR because it can change independently of kidney function (variable urea production and passive reabsorption of filtered urea); changes in BUN are therefore not recommended for detecting changes in kidney function or kidney injury.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND Standard Safety Tables and Figures, Kidney Injury TAG v1.2): marketing applications with a potential kidney injury signal or kidney injury as an AESI; informative for applicants, not binding on them

rows.quote:
Although blood urea nitrogen (BUN) varies inversely with kidney function, it is a less useful indicator than serum creatinine or eGFR because
BUN can change independently of kidney function. The two main reasons are: (1) the rate of urea production is not constant (e.g., production
increases with high-protein diet, hemorrhage, trauma, or glucocorticoids, and decreases with a low-protein diet or liver disease); and (2) filtered
urea is passively reabsorbed by the kidney, leading to a rise in BUN that is disproportionate to the change in kidney function in some clinical
situations (e.g., volume depletion). It is therefore not recommended that changes in BUN be used to detect changes in kidney function or kidney
injury.

f.statement: The last on-treatment value is the last value of a laboratory parameter obtained within a specific time frame (for example 1 to 3 half-lives) after treatment discontinuation, whatever the reason for discontinuation; it therefore covers subjects who completed the trial as well as those who stopped treatment for other reasons.

rows.quote:
For Table 6: Subjects With Last On-Treatment Creatinine and eGFR Value by Level
Criteria by Treatment Arm, the “last on-treatment value” is defined as the last value for
any given laboratory parameter obtained within a specific timeframe (e.g., 1 to 3 half-
lives) following treatment discontinuation, regardless of the reason for discontinuation.
Therefore, this table includes subjects who completed the trial and thus discontinued
treatment per protocol as well as subjects who discontinued treatment for other
reasons. This presentation can be helpful if a study drug causes laboratory
abnormalities but the effect is diminished because multiple labs are obtained when
subjects are no longer receiving the study drug.

The following analyses may be performed to further explore changes in kidney
laboratory studies over time. Analyses may explore a single laboratory value or show a
trend over time. Note that variability could be present in populations with variable kidney

or injury (e.g., cystatin C, quantitative measures of proteinuria or albuminuria), these
data should also be analyzed.

f.title: Compare kidney values with the last known value to detect acute injury and assess reversibility
f.statement: Analysing change relative to the last known value may be more helpful than comparison with baseline for short-term changes reflecting acute or drug-induced kidney injury. Comparison with baseline does not distinguish acute from chronic injury; additional analyses may be needed to follow up potential signals and to assess reversibility.

f.statement: In the percent change from baseline display of serum creatinine, when a subject has several values (scheduled and unscheduled) for a visit, the worst value (the maximum increase in creatinine) is shown at the pre-specified scheduled visit.

f.title: Select subjects for graphical patient profiles together with CDS
f.statement: A graphical patient profile (GPP) combines a subject's drug exposure, AEs, concomitant therapies and relevant laboratory values over time. Not all subjects need one; the clinical reviewer should work with CDS to select subjects, for example all subjects with kidney injury per the Kidney Injury OCMQs, or a subset of subjects who received the investigational drug.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND Standard Safety Tables and Figures, Kidney Injury TAG v1.2): marketing applications with a potential kidney injury signal or kidney injury as an AESI; informative for applicants, not binding on them

rows.quote:
A graphical patient profile (GPP) displays subject-level data over time to provide an
overview of a subject’s course by combining drug exposure, AEs, concomitant
therapies, and relevant lab values. Note that not all subjects will need a GPP. The
clinical reviewer should work with the CDS to identify appropriate subjects for this type
of display. For instance, a GPP may be helpful for all subjects who experienced kidney
injury during the trial based on the Kidney Injury OCMQs, or for only a subset of
subjects who received the investigational drug.

f.title: eGFR equations: CKD-EPI for adults, Schwartz (2009) for ages 1 to <18, serum creatinine by age under 1
f.statement: eGFR is calculated with the CKD-EPI creatinine equation for adults (18 years and over) and the Schwartz (2009) equation for children aged 1 to under 18; for children under 1 year there is no applicable eGFR equation and serum creatinine by age cut-offs is used. A subject enrolled before age 18 should stay on the Schwartz equation for the whole study even after turning 18.
